skill.name: using-sops
skill.description: Manage sops-encrypted dotenv secrets through a repository wrapper, including development workflows, production elevation, key setup, and rotation.
skill.summary: Work with sops and age secrets through a repository's pnpm secrets wrapper.
skill.author: jssblck

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally grants agents broad access to encrypted development secrets and supports persistent production elevation. The most serious design stores a shared private key in persistent cloud environment variables, creating cross-project credential exposure.

remediation.issue: Agents may reveal or change all development secrets without confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before showing, changing, deleting, or passing secrets to a command. Default to key names and redacted values.

remediation.issue: A single agent identity decrypts development secrets across all projects.
remediation.suggestion: Create per-project, short-lived agent identities with least privilege. Rotate existing recipients after removing the shared identity.

remediation.issue: Reusable private keys are stored in persistent non-secret cloud variables.
remediation.suggestion: Use a supported secret store or short-lived brokered credential. Do not install credentials where platform guidance says they can be exposed.

remediation.issue: Production elevation persists until manual file deletion.
remediation.suggestion: Use memory-backed, session-bound elevation with automatic expiry and cleanup. Require fresh user approval for each production operation.

remediation.issue: Installation commands execute downloaded binaries without integrity checks.
remediation.suggestion: Publish expected SHA-256 checksums or signature verification steps. Download archives before extraction and stop when verification fails.

semantic_findings.title: Unprompted Bulk Development Secret Access
semantic_findings.description: The skill authorizes agents to show, modify, delete, and execute with all development secrets without user confirmation. This can expose or corrupt credentials beyond the immediate task.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction explicitly says agents may manage development secrets without asking and includes a command that reveals everything decrypted.

semantic_findings.title: Shared Cross-Project Decryption Identity
semantic_findings.description: One agent private key is shared across every project and installed for all agent sessions. Compromise of one machine or session exposes every development file using that recipient.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both files explicitly describe a user-wide identity shared by every project and accessible to any agent session on the machine.

semantic_findings.title: Private Key Stored in Non-Secret Cloud Variables
semantic_findings.description: The setup places a reusable age private key in persistent cloud environment variables, including fields documented as unsuitable for credentials. Redaction limitations are acknowledged.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly require SOPS_AGE_KEY in persistent environment variables and state that one platform advises against credentials there.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Production Elevation Artifact
semantic_findings.description: Production elevation remains active until a checkout file is manually deleted. A stale or copied checkout can retain production decryption access longer than intended.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow states that elevation persists until manual deletion and has no timeout, session binding, or automatic cleanup.

content.value_statement: Encrypted repository secrets require careful commands, keys, and environment handling. This skill guides SOPS workflows through an existing pnpm secrets wrapper.
actual_capabilities: Recognizes repositories that use .sops.yaml and encrypted environment files.
Guides development secret viewing, retrieval, updates, and deletion through pnpm secrets.
Runs child processes with decrypted environment values through the repository wrapper.
Explains user-assisted production elevation and checkout-specific access.
Guides SOPS and age installation, identity setup, project initialization, and key rotation.
limitations: Requires an existing pnpm secrets wrapper and repository conventions.
Requires installed SOPS and age binaries plus a valid recipient private key.
Cannot access production secrets without an authorized key and user-assisted elevation.
Cloud key storage guidance creates serious exposure risks and needs stronger controls.

use_cases.title: Update Development Configuration
use_cases.description: Inspect or change an encrypted development variable through the repository wrapper.

use_cases.title: Configure Deployment Secrets
use_cases.description: Prepare production decryption and service startup while keeping the key outside application files.

use_cases.title: Rotate SOPS Recipients
use_cases.description: Replace a lost or compromised age recipient and re-encrypt affected secret files.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect One Development Variable
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the repository secrets wrapper to retrieve [VARIABLE] from development. Explain the command first and avoid displaying unrelated values.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Development Secret
prompt_templates.prompt: Add [VARIABLE] to the development secrets and environment schema. Confirm before changing files and report any environment you cannot decrypt.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Command With Secrets
prompt_templates.prompt: Run [COMMAND] with development secrets through the repository wrapper. Verify the command scope and do not print decrypted values.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Recipient Rotation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the SOPS recipients for [PROJECT]. Propose a rotation plan for [COMPROMISED_RECIPIENT], including affected files, approvals, re-encryption, and credential replacement.

output_examples.input: Retrieve the development Stripe key without showing other secrets.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies the repository wrapper, requests confirmation, retrieves only the named value, and avoids echoing unrelated decrypted data.

output_examples.input: Add a required API endpoint to every accessible environment.
output: The development secret and environment schema are updated.
Production remains unchanged because elevation is unavailable.
The deployment requirement is recorded for review.

output_examples.output: The assistant lists recipient replacement, file re-encryption, value rotation, deployment updates, verification, and encrypted history exposure.

best_practices: Use the repository wrapper instead of calling SOPS directly.
Request approval before revealing, changing, or executing with any secret.
Rotate both recipients and decrypted values after a private key leak.
anti_patterns: Do not print complete decrypted files when one variable is sufficient.
Do not place personal or production private keys in tracked files, logs, or cloud agent environments.
Do not leave production elevation active after the approved operation.

faq.question: What repository layout does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects .sops.yaml, encrypted secrets files, and a pnpm secrets wrapper such as tools/secrets.ts.

faq.question: Can it work without an age private key?
faq.answer: It can create files for configured public recipients, but decryption and editing require an authorized private key.

faq.question: Does it call SOPS directly?
faq.answer: It instructs agents to use the repository wrapper when one exists.

faq.question: How are production secrets protected?
faq.answer: Production uses a project-specific identity and requires checkout elevation. The documented elevation remains active until manually removed.

faq.question: Can it rotate a compromised recipient?
faq.answer: It guides recipient replacement, SOPS updatekeys, commit review, and rotation of every value exposed by the old key.

faq.question: Is cloud agent key storage safe?
faq.answer: The documented environment-variable approach is high risk. Use scoped, short-lived credentials in a supported secret store instead.
